subject: SLO & load portrait clarification and next steps
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: SLO & load portrait clarifications

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a short list of items we need to size and validate Redwood Dedicated for your use case: 

1) Latency SLOs: what are your target p50/p95/p99 for single-turn streaming responses and for full-response completion? Please indicate separate targets if streaming (token-by-token) vs non-streaming.

2) Throughput profile: please confirm steady-state QPS and peak QPS. If you can, provide tokens/sec or average tokens per request. We need both:
   - Typical steady-state QPS and mean tokens/request
   - Expected peak QPS (burst window) and duration (minutes/hours)

3) Concurrency: how many concurrent sessions/users do you expect to be actively generating at burst?

4) Streaming requirements: do you require sub-200ms first-token latency for streaming? Any constrained jitter SLA?

5) Request shape: token length distribution (P10/P50/P90), percentage of multi-turn chat calls vs single-turn summarization calls.

6) Any prefixes or long-context KV cache reuse (e.g., same conversation reused across many requests)?

I attached a simple CSV template you can fill — acme_load_summary.csv — with columns for timestamped sample windows if you have historical traces. If not, a best-effort estimate is totally fine.

Next steps / timeline: if you can return the CSV and a filled SLO matrix, we’ll run a sizing sketch and follow up with a recommended configuration (GPU pool size, batching/queueing targets, and streaming tuning) within 48 business hours.

Thanks — looping in Marissa and Vanessa for ops/telemetry and performance checks.

—
Laura Bennett
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com

Attachment: acme_load_summary.csv (csv, stub)
Attachment: acme_slo_matrix.xlsx (xlsx, stub)

From: Samir Patel <samir@acme.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Watanabe <lisa.w@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: SLO & load portrait clarifications

Laura — thanks, appreciated. Quick responses inline below and I've attached our preliminary export. More detail from infra team coming later this week.

> 1) Latency SLOs
We are aiming for: streaming first-token p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 300ms. Completion latency (full response) p95 <= 1.8s for typical 150-300 token outputs. Some longer generations up to 1,200 tokens are ok at higher p95 (3-4s).

> 2) Throughput profile
Steady-state: ~18 QPS with mean 240 tokens/request (these are mostly short chat replies).
Peak bursts: up to 420 QPS for ~6 minute windows during daily batch-apply and campaign spikes. Peak tokens/sec estimate: ~100k tokens/sec at peak.

> 3) Concurrency
Active concurrent generating sessions during peak: ~1,100 across global frontends (US primarily).

> 4) Streaming requirements
Yes — first-token <= 200ms desired. jitter tolerance: occasional 20-30ms variability fine, but we need a 99% window within 500ms.

> 5) Request shape
Token length: P10 45 tokens, P50 220 tokens, P90 540 tokens. Multi-turn chat is ~72% of calls; summarization/batch jobs ~28%.

> 6) Context reuse
We typically reuse ~30% of requests with a hot prefix (same conversation reused).

Attaching acme_load_summary.csv (exported sample from our proxy) — it has 1-min rollups for a recent 48hr window.

Samir
Director of Product, Acme AI
samir@acme.ai

Attachment: acme_load_summary.csv (csv, 2.1MB stub)

Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: SLO & load portrait clarifications

Samir — this is great, thanks for the quick data dump. Attaching the file you provided into our sizing doc.

Internal note to Rishi / Marissa / Vanessa: please review the peak characterization — 420 QPS with ~100k tokens/sec peak and 1,100 concurrent sessions. Two things to validate:
  - Streaming path: confirm whether we can meet p50=120ms, p95=300ms at that concurrency with conservative batching and prefix cache reuse.
  - Resource profile: for a first pass I expect a mixed pool with streaming-optimized instances plus a small set of high-throughput quantized instances for the bulk requests.

Rishi — can you sketch a quick baseline (ballpark GPU count and memory footprint) for these numbers? Marissa — please call out telemetry hooks we'd need from Acme to catch regressions early (example: per-route token latency histograms and burst window sampling).

Samir / Lisa — next actions we propose:
1) Redwood provides an initial sizing doc and recommended config (by EoD Thu).
2) Acme confirms whether they want canary routing for 2-week trial (we recommend yes).
3) If okay, we follow with a 2-week performance validation run in Dedicated.

If any of the numbers above shift (especially peak QPS or concurrency), flag here and we'll re-run the sketch.

Thanks —
Laura

Thanks — read through the numbers. Quick technical assessments and proposed mutual action plan (MAP):

Assessment:
- 420 QPS peak @ ~100k tokens/sec and 1,100 concurrency is high but fits a hybrid approach: allocate ~70% of steady throughput to quantized high-throughput nodes and keep ~30% on streaming-optimized nodes to meet first-token targets.
- Hot-prefix reuse (30%) gives a sizable KV cache win and will reduce amplification during bursts.

Proposed MAP / next steps (owners & ETA):
1) Sizing sketch (Rishi) — rough GPU footprint and memory matrix with two configs: conservative and optimized (1 business day).
   Owner: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com — ETA: Mon 21 Jun 2027 EOD.
2) Telemetry checklist (Marissa) — list of per-route metrics + ingestion hooks we need from Acme.
   Owner: marissa_cole@redwood.com — ETA: Mon 21 Jun 2027 noon PT.
3) Canary plan & SLA guardrails (Laura) — propose rollout steps and fallback policies for Dedicated trial.
   Owner: laura_bennett@redwood.com — ETA: Tue 22 Jun 2027.
4) Procurement intro (Marissa + Laura) — surface initial commercial terms for a 2-week trial and options for reserved commit if validation meets SLOs.
   Owner: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com — ETA: Wed 23 Jun 2027.

Immediate ask for Acme: please confirm whether the 420 QPS peak is per-region or global aggregated (Samir if you can confirm), and whether the 6-minute burst is a hard upper bound or an illustrative window. Those two answers materially affect the number of streaming nodes we hold warm.

I will start the sizing sketch today and include notes on batching windows, max queue latency, and recommended quantization profiles.

—
Rishi Malhotra
